newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil parallel bond to carry five-year maturity.
newsitem.headline: Brazil parallel bond to carry five-year maturity.

text.p: The Central Bank said Brazil's upcoming sovereign parallel bond would carry a five-year maturity in each of three European currencies in which it will be denominated.

"The transaction comprises the simultaneous issues of bonds denominated in Dutch guilders, French francs and Austrian schillings... All three issues will have a five-year maturity," the bank said in a statement.
It said volume, price and launch date would be determined later.
The Central Bank said ING Bank was managing the guilder issue, Paribras was managing the franc issue and Creditanstalt was managing the schilling issue.
All three issues will be fungible, or redenominated, to the euro when the European currency is launched in 1999, the Central Bank said.
A representative at one of the co-managing banks said the roadshow for the bond would begin on April 22, next Tuesday.

Traders said there has not been a lot of price talk about the new issue because it is the first time Brazil has issued in any one of the currencies. It would also be the first parallel bond issued by an emerging market nation.
For comparison purposes, however, market players point to Brazil's five-year 8-7/8 percent global, which priced at 265 basis points over Treasuries, but is now trading at 195 bps over.
